posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body:
I know it doesn't have to do with your resource request, but I notice you specify for some reason that you own RPG Maker 1.5. You should strongly consider upgrading your project - it fixes bugs in the engine, and newer plugins you look at might not be compatible with 1.5's code.
(also, just a quick note - I'm sure everyone will understand you, but I dunno where you got ATP: the included assets are referred to as the RTP)
Good luck with your project.

posts.author: Avery
posts.body:
For the sprites and the SV battlers, with this tutorial you should be able to at least do the black recolors easily (or after a reasonable learning time):
Recoloring Pixel Art
Can you make proper recolors?  Yes No What do you mean with “proper”?   While dedicated beginners as 15 year old me back then are able to recolor pixelated sprites with MS Paint, that is very much noch recommended.  For this tutorial I will use Gimp, it is free, powerful and can do all the...
forums.rpgmakerweb.com
Here is all you need to know about recoloring the faces, again, this might have a learning curve, probably steeper than the one before, but nonetheless it is something very doable:
Adding patterns and in depth talk about layer masks
When I make tutorials I often use “layer masks” which are probably something that is not the most beginner friendly thing in the world. Not because they are difficult to use, just because they are a concept that might be a bit difficult to wrap your head around if you never heard of it. So even...
forums.rpgmakerweb.com
Recoloring patterns into pixel art is a bit more difficult - well not really, I think it is more a "wrap your brian around it"-thing. I like to simply recolor the character I need with a pattern in all the colors the pattern will consist of, and then I - e.g. in graphicsgale - pixelate the pattern carefully onto the "base pose" (on an extra layer of course), e.g. stripes, just in a solid color. The "movements" I try to edit from that base so they match and I just do that for all directions, poses, etc. Then all I need to do is to use my pixelated layer as base for a selection and remove that from the color that I need the stripes in.
Sidenote: you might not have noticed, but people cannot edit my faceset and SV battler here and post it for you, that is against my terms of use.
It also confuses me that you look at the stuff I made for requests but didn't even bother to check my resource thread since there are half of the things you are looking for anyways:
